subject.title: [Bug]: Config validator rejects mediaLocalRoots despite type definitions supporting it (Telegram outbound)

question: Should OpenClaw expose configurable outbound local media roots for Telegram/media sends, and if yes, should the canonical surface be a broad filesystem policy such as `tools.fs.roots` or a narrower channel/media-specific config key?
rationale: The missing key is source-provable, but the fix would add new configuration that controls which host paths can be read and uploaded through channels, so automation should not choose the permanent security/product boundary.

options.title: Use one canonical media-root policy
options.body: Settle the cross-channel/file-tool contract first, then implement one schema/runtime/docs/test path that covers Telegram and sibling media surfaces.

options.title: Add a narrow Telegram key
options.body: Expose `channels.telegram.mediaLocalRoots` only for Telegram outbound media, accepting the risk of a channel-specific escape hatch that may later need consolidation.

options.title: Keep staged-media only
options.body: Do not add new roots and instead document the current managed media/workspace staging workflow as the supported security boundary.

recommendation.title: Use one canonical media-root policy
recommendation.body: Settle the cross-channel/file-tool contract first, then implement one schema/runtime/docs/test path that covers Telegram and sibling media surfaces.

likelyOwner.reason: Current blame and recent history put the central media root, config schema, and gateway send surfaces under this contributor's recent work.
